Let me ask this: if the "Deep-Roots" theory is false, and war was rare during the paleolithic era, then why does it seem that every modern hunter-gather tribe we encounter, including those that have little to no contact with modern civilization, have elements of language and culture specifically centered around war? The problem here is that they are using stupid tricks of language, rather than evidence to support their case. Just because paleolithic people didn't take a bunch of machine guns and mow each other down in a field doesn't mean they weren't going to war. "War" can have various meanings and interpretations in different contexts but it essentially boils down to the same basic thing:

First, we know from observing modern hunter-gatherers that their form of "war" is inherently less violent than our form of "war". It's still generally the same thing, i.e. a fight over land and resources. However, for many tribes this can mean mounting a series of raids between several tribes where they run in, grab each other's women and resources, and run out. Violence is an aspect of this, but the "invading" tribe can usually accomplish their goal (or realize they will fail) without too much damage to either side. It's no different than when a pair of billy goats head-butt each other over a mate. They don't need to kill each other before they've realized whose won and whose lost, and considering they don't have the support of modern medicine (like we do) it's usually better to back away before too much damage is done and you've compromised your chance of survival. In fact, this form of war was the basis for the freaking Illiad, one of the famous WAR stories in all of history

Two groups (tribes, noble house, mob families, etc.) going to war with each other over the death of one of the group's members at the hands of another groups members? Again, look at Romeo and Juliet, a famous story about two WARRING houses whose inspiration was taken from numerous historically similar accounts. Or, for a more recent example you could look at the Italian mafia in the early 20th century US, whose groups were constantly going to war with each other. It may not be war in the modern sense of two nation-states bombing the hell out of each other, but it is war none-the-less.
